newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-KJUS SITS OUT DOWNHILL TO PROTEST SCHEDULE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-KJUS SITS OUT DOWNHILL TO PROTEST SCHEDULE.

text.p: Lasse Kjus, last year's World Cup overall champion, pulled out of the men's downhill on Tuesday to protest against the exhausting World Cup schedule.
The Norwegian said he skipped the training runs for Wednesday's race because of a gruelling stretch that sent him to three continents in three weeks.
"I rather prefer to focus on some events here because I don't feel able to perform at my best if I race also in the downhill," he said.
Kjus won the downhill at Kvitfjell, Norway, and was third in the Super-G there two weeks ago before heading to Japan last week for technical races at the site of next year's Olympics.
He fell out of both the slalom and giant slalom at Shiga Kogen before travelling to Vail for this week's World Cup Finals.
The 26-year-old Kjus, who won world championship silvers in the downhill, Super-G and giant slalom at Sestriere, said he would write a formal complaint to the FIS over the scheduling.
